Publish from SolidWorks (product CAD)#

**Status: 4.0.0-beta.1 — skeleton; the logic is unit-tested, the add-in needs a real SolidWorks install to build and run.** PublishCore.cs — what to export, the units check, the upload with progress and cancel, every error sentence — ran against a mock SolidWorks host, and a GLB and an IFC it exported were published to a real local Verse server and finished (web/test/fix-verify-aec.mjs). The add-in shell (SwAddin.cs, SwHost.cs, the forms) compiles only against the SolidWorks interop assemblies, which come with SolidWorks — it has **not been compiled or run here. STEP is not uploaded: the server cannot build CAD STEP yet** (below).

A Verse command group (menu and toolbar) in SolidWorks: **Publish to Verse** exports the active part or assembly and uploads it with progress; the share link is copied and opened — a link that opens on any phone.

You need: SolidWorks 2019 or newer, Windows x64.

1. Build and install#

Download VersePublish-SolidWorks-4.0.0-beta.1.zip from the downloads page and unzip it. The package is source until it is built on a machine with SolidWorks (the interop DLLs are referenced from the install and never shipped):

Code
sh integrations/aec/solidworks/make_package.sh   # -> dist/VersePublish-SolidWorks-4.0.0-beta.1.zip (source)
# on Windows with SolidWorks and the .NET SDK:
dotnet build -c Release -p:SolidWorksApi="C:\Program Files\SOLIDWORKS Corp\SOLIDWORKS\api\redist"

Then, in an administrator prompt:

Code
%WINDIR%\Microsoft.NET\Framework64\v4.0.30319\RegAsm.exe /codebase VersePublishSolidWorks.dll

and tick Verse Publish under Tools ▸ Add-Ins. RegAsm /u removes it.

2. Server and key#

Verse settings… — server URL (default https://verse.ctruh.com), API key, account token, export as (auto / glb / ifc), bake lighting, open the link when done, and Use … for every Verse plug-in.

Nothing is compiled in. Settings live in the per-user %APPDATA%\Ctruh\VersePublish\settings.json every Verse plug-in shares, solidworks section. VERSE_SERVER, VERSE_API_KEY, VERSE_TOKEN override it.

3. Publish#

  1. Open a part or an assembly (the command is disabled for drawings) and choose Publish to Verse.
  2. A progress window shows uploading % → building stages; Cancel stops it and tells you whether anything was published.
  3. Published! — the link is on the clipboard and opens in the browser.

Success looks like: Published! with the link (also on the clipboard, and opened in the browser); a 250 mm part measures 0.25 m in the viewer.

What gets exported#

  • auto (default): GLB through SolidWorks' own Save As when your version offers glTF/GLB; otherwise IFC (SolidWorks' IFC 2x3 / IFC 4 export). The server builds IFC into one clickable object per product with its properties — Publish IFC.
  • Units. SolidWorks reports the model's size in metres. The GLB is measured against it; if the exporter wrote millimetres (or cm, inches, feet), the scene is wrapped in one metre-scale root node — a 250 mm block measures 0.25 m in the link. IFC carries its own units.
  • Appearances become glTF materials as SolidWorks' exporter writes them; decals and RealView-only effects do not carry over.

STEP and the server-side CAD path#

Not available yet — nothing here pretends otherwise. The Verse server converts glTF, FBX, OBJ, IFC, USD, splats and point clouds; it has **no B-rep / CAD kernel**, so it cannot tessellate STEP (AP203 / AP214 / AP242), IGES, Parasolid or native SolidWorks files. A STEP file even begins with the same ISO-10303-21 line as IFC, so the server would try to read it as a building model and fail with a confusing IFC error. Every Verse upload helper (Python, Ruby, C#, JavaScript) now refuses those files before uploading, with: "Verse cannot build STEP files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."

Next step (not built): a server-side step → glb converter beside tools/ifc-convert — an Open CASCADE-based tessellator (for example occt-import-js, WASM, LGPL-2.1 with the OCCT exception — licence review needed) behind X-Verse-Kind: step, with the sniffer telling STEP from IFC by FILE_SCHEMA (AUTOMOTIVE_DESIGN / AP242_… vs. IFC2X3 / IFC4), one node per product with its name, chordal tolerance chosen from the model size, then the ordinary mesh road. Until then: GLB or IFC from the add-in.

Troubleshooting#

Every problem ends in one sentence; the first words tell you which row applies.

You seeWhat it meansDo this
"Could not reach the Verse server at …"Wrong server URL, no internet, or a firewall / proxy blocking the plug-in.Check Server URL in Verse ▸ Verse settings… (default https://verse.ctruh.com) and open it in a browser.
"The Verse server at … did not recognise the account token …"The token is mistyped, was revoked, or belongs to another server. Nothing was uploaded.Copy the token again from Studio, or clear it to publish without an account.
"The server did not accept your API key or account token …"This server only takes uploads with an API key; the sentence ends with its reason.Enter the key from the server's operator in Verse ▸ Verse settings….
"Upload limit reached: …"The hourly upload limit, or the API key's daily quota.Wait as the sentence says, or add an account token from Studio (a higher limit).
"The server is busy right now. …" / "The server is out of storage. …"The server's build queue or disk is full. Your file is fine.Publish again in a few minutes.
"The upload kept failing …"The connection dropped again and again.Publish again when the connection is steady; a large upload continues where it stopped.
"Verse cannot build … files yet. Export the model as GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that file instead."STEP / IGES / native CAD files are not built by the server yet.Export GLB (or FBX / OBJ) and publish that.
"Stopped waiting for the server. The scene is still being built …"You cancelled after the upload; the server keeps building.The scene appears in your Verse dashboard (with an account token) when it is ready.
"Drawings have no 3D model to publish. …"The command works on parts and assemblies.Open the part or assembly instead.
Verse Publish missing in Tools ▸ Add-InsThe DLL was not registered for COM.RegAsm /codebase VersePublishSolidWorks.dll from an administrator prompt, then restart SolidWorks.

Anything else: send the whole sentence (and, for a build error, the scene name) to hello@ctruh.com.

What has been tested#

Export choice (GLB → IFC fallback, forced GLB / IFC, STEP refused), drawing / no document / empty part sentences, GLB unit check (mm, in, metres), settings, dead server, cancel — mock SolidWorks hosttested
The mock host's GLB and IFC published to a real local server, scenes donetested
Compiling the add-in shell; registration, menus, Save As to GLB (which versions offer it) and IFC, the bounding box calls, the forms inside SolidWorksneeds a real install
